functional_semantics.triton: out[row] = first index of the row maximum; int64 (M,) output; dim=1 path uses x.contiguous() (impl_triton.py 14-29, 48-54).
functional_semantics.cutile: Same: running (best_val, best_idx) per row, int64 (M,) output, x.contiguous() for dim=1 (impl_cutile.py 28-44, 54-61).
functional_semantics.note: Both realise torch.argmax(x, dim=1) (impl_torch.py 5); the generator always passes dim=1 (tensors.py 456-458). Both also carry a dim != 1 transpose-copy branch (impl_triton.py 51, impl_cutile.py 57) that the benchmark never takes.

stages.triton: torch.empty int64 output (54) then one launch with grid (M,) (impl_triton.py 56-65).
stages.cutile: torch.empty int64 output (61), host-computed chunk count passed as a compile-time constant (85-88), one launch with grid (M,1,1) (impl_cutile.py 90-92).
stages.note: Identical single-kernel, one-program-per-row structure; the compile-time chunk count on one side is a mapping choice.

dependencies.triton: Rows independent; sequential chunk loop inside a program (impl_triton.py 17-27).
dependencies.note: No cross-program merge on either side.

reduction_scan_sort.triton: Chunks in increasing column order; tl.max + tl.argmax per chunk (Triton default tie_break_left gives the lowest index); cross-chunk merge with strict tile_max > best_val so the earlier chunk wins ties; best_idx = start + tile_arg in int64 (impl_triton.py 17-27).
reduction_scan_sort.cutile: Chunks in increasing column order; ct.max + ct.argmax per chunk; identical strict > merge; best_idx = start + tile_arg in int64 (impl_cutile.py 31-42).
reduction_scan_sort.note: Same scan structure and merge rule. The in-chunk tie-breaking of ct.argmax is not stated in source; the contract requires the reference's first-occurrence rule, which the strict cross-chunk merge satisfies whenever the in-chunk primitive returns the lowest index. Not a divergence in algorithmic content; randn inputs make exact ties essentially unobservable.

precision.triton: Each chunk loaded with other=-inf and cast to fp32 before comparison; best_val fp32; indices int64 (impl_triton.py 14-15, 20-23).
precision.cutile: Chunk loaded with PaddingMode.NEG_INF and cast to fp32; best_val fp32; indices int64 (impl_cutile.py 28-29, 33-38).
precision.note: Same: exact fp32 upcast for comparisons, -inf padding, int64 indices.

preprocessing.triton: x.contiguous() (no-op for the generator's input) and an output allocation; the dim != 1 transpose copy is inside run() but unreached (impl_triton.py 46-54).
preprocessing.cutile: Same (impl_cutile.py 52-61), plus host arithmetic for the chunk count (85-88).
preprocessing.note: No device-side preprocessing for the benchmark path; nothing cached.

intermediate_storage.cutile: None; running pair in tile scalars (impl_cutile.py 28-29).

mutation.triton: No input written; output freshly allocated (impl_triton.py 54).
mutation.cutile: No input written; output freshly allocated (impl_cutile.py 61).

fq_boundary.note: config.yaml 17-18. Counts one read of x and one compare per element, which is exactly the single kernel's work; the 8*M-byte int64 output write is omitted and negligible for N >= 1024. Neither run() copies x on the dim=1 path, so the timed boundary matches on both sides.
